title: Choose the Ripple Out visual world
question: Your steer, oceanic, clean, minimal and modern, now binds every card. The roll assigned Sea Glass. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Sea Glass
options.lineage: Sea glass: broken glass the waves carry for years and wash up, smooth and frosted, on every shore.
options.thesis: Each song is a piece of sea glass the setlist carries out to whoever opens it: worn smooth, frosted, quietly coloured.
options.viewport: Songs as numbered sea-glass pieces along a foam tideline, word-labelled controls, and a calm lyric column with chords tinted by their glass colour.
options.risk: Frosted pieces can slide into glassmorphism or pebble-cute if they get blur, shine or tilt, so they stay flat, matte and on the grid.

raised.raise: Rank is inversion: the song being sung is the only solid piece; every other song stays frosted outline.
The lyric column is the one calm panel; colour lives only in the frame and the chords.
Nothing touches: one constant gap between every element, so the page breathes at TV distance.
Every control says what it does in words (Chords, Key, Split); no unexplained icons.

options.label: The Set
options.lineage: Surf swell forecasts: waves arrive in sets, drawn as clean bar charts with period and direction.
options.thesis: A setlist is a set of waves; each song is one wave rolling in, charted like a clean swell forecast.
options.viewport: A swell chart where each bar is a song in the set and the one being sung is crest teal, with key and tempo set as forecast data above the lyrics.
options.risk: Familiar: it reads like the weather and dashboard apps people already use, and a white ground is bright on a TV at night.

options.label: Plane Wave
options.lineage: Ikko Tanaka's posters: a figure rebuilt from a few flat planes on a quiet grid.
options.thesis: The wave is built from the songs: each song is one flat plane of ocean colour, and together they crest.
options.viewport: A cresting wave of four flat planes, one per song, with the current song's plane in the accent colour, over a strictly gridded reading column.
options.case: Holds identification: it is exactly your 'clean, minimal, modern', and the songs literally form the wave. Narrowly loses on clarity, because planes are more abstract than numbered pieces.
options.risk: A light ground glares on a TV at night, and the planes become decoration if they stop mapping to songs.

options.label: Deep Dive
options.lineage: A dive down an ocean wall: the turquoise surface, a cold thermocline, then the deep.
options.thesis: The setlist as a descent: each song is a depth stop, the one being sung lit by a single thermocline band.
options.viewport: A vertical depth axis with songs as depth stops, a cyan band across the current song, and lyrics in chalk white beside it.
options.case: Beats the roll on clarity, because one lit band on a vertical axis is unmistakable. Loses on identification, because worship isn't a descent and divers are a niche.
options.risk: Deep dark plus one cyan band edges toward the stage and concert look you ruled out.

options.label: Depot Blind
options.lineage: Bus destination blinds: dyed cloth courses stepping under one window.
options.thesis: Songs as cloth courses stepping under a fixed window.
options.viewport: A green cloth blind showing the current song under a window.
options.case: Declined: bottle green and chrome yellow break your oceanic steer, and transit cloth isn't your audience's world.
options.kept: Rank is inversion: the lead item alone prints solid.

options.label: Festival Hoarding
options.lineage: Screenprinted street-fair flyers pasted over each other.
options.thesis: A collage of flat colour with one calm white panel on top.
options.viewport: A loud collage with a white panel floating over it.
options.case: Declined: loud and playful, the opposite of clean, minimal and oceanic.
options.kept: When the frame is busy, the reading column is the one calm panel.

options.label: Tensegrity Column
options.lineage: Carbon rods held apart by red cord.
options.thesis: Songs as members of a balanced force network.
options.viewport: A breathing column of rods with force labels.
options.case: Declined: engineering and red cord, nothing oceanic and nothing worshipful.
options.kept: Nothing touches: every element keeps its distance.

options.label: Napkin Zine
options.lineage: Hand-drawn explainer zines with mascots and marker.
options.thesis: Songs explained like a friend's napkin sketch.
options.viewport: A doodled setlist with a mascot pointing at the song.
options.case: Declined: mascots and marker are the 'too playful' you ruled out.
options.kept: Explain like a friend: every control says what it does in words.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean chord-sheet app in the OnSong and Planning Center mould, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: A song list bar, key controls, and black lyrics with blue chords on white.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other chord app by design, and nothing in it says 'ripple out'.
